question:
A manufacturer finds the demand for a product as $p=100-2x$, $x$ is quantity. Cost function: $C(x)=32x+1200$.

(a) Express profit in $x$.

(b) Find $x$ and $p$ for max profit.

(c) Confirm with both first and second derivative tests.

options.A:
(a) $P(x)=68x+2x^2-1200$
(b) Maximum profit occurs at $x=17$ and $p=66$.
(c) $P''=4>0$, so it is a minimum.
options.B:
(a) $P(x)=100x-2x^2-1200$
(b) Maximum profit occurs at $x=25$ and $p=50$.
(c) $P''=-4<0$, so it is a maximum.
options.C:
(a) $P(x)=68x-2x^2+1200$
(b) Maximum profit occurs at $x=34$ and $p=32$.
(c) $P'(x)$ changes from negative to positive, so it is a minimum.
options.D:
(a) $P(x)=68x-2x^2-1200$
(b) Maximum profit occurs at $x=17$ and $p=66$.
(c) $P'(x)$ changes from positive to negative at $x=17$, and $P''=-4<0$, confirming maximum.
